_provenance: Measured on 2026-11-22 in the course authoring container: Docker Engine 29.10.0 (BuildKit), python:3.12-slim (index digest sha256:5e2bdb1b0d54...), x86_64, a shared and busy host. Builds used a copy of python:3.12-slim with the sandbox proxy's CA certificate added (one extra 201 kB layer and three ENV lines) so pip could reach PyPI; without that environment quirk your image is about 0.2 MB smaller. Timings depend on the machine and its load; the RATIOS are the lesson.

context_experiment._note: A copy of the lab with 300 MB of data/raw, 40 MB of runs/, 20 MB of .git and a .venv added (344 MB on disk). Dockerfile with COPY . . before pip install.
context_experiment._sizes_note: image_disk_mb is the DISK USAGE column of `docker image ls` (Docker 29, containerd image store); image_content_mb is CONTENT SIZE: the compressed layers that are pushed and pulled. The 360 MB of junk is random bytes, which do not compress.
